scope: Reviewed actual temporary Common config/launch metadata/logs and native source paths; no IPC call, DB open, nodekey read or process mutation.

findings.conclusion: NoDiscovery disables both ordinary discovery and the eth DNS candidate iterator; static/trusted/bootstrap sets empty. Native browser mesh candidates retain their mesh transport identity.

AutoRole enables Common RPC bridge while native ingress Enabled remains false. This is transaction submission plus authenticated receipt delivery, not block/header synchronization. Start returns before UDP ingress listener when Enabled=false; live log records http3rpc=false and initial outbox records/bytes=0. No block/header insertion or downloader delivery occurs in the audited TxQUIC file.
findings.limitation: Initial outbox=0 is a log observation, not packet capture for the entire test.

findings.conclusion: Normal ReconfigBackend.Start is a no-op. MinerStart invokes Service.start; the recorded launch requests no mining. Even an explicit non-committee start returns before configuring and starting authenticated consensus transport. netService.StartStop(true) is what calls server.Start. Creating a service and its log message do not establish an active consensus participant.

Native header/body responses enter downloader through the established native eth peer. Actual report observes temporary Common peers only with transport browser-mesh; only owned A/B then C/B browser labels. OFF leaves peer/circuit/queue zero and stable RTC counters.
Temporary source config is mesh-only; no keyId/signingKeyPath. The source-uplink API allowlist is config/status/session/renew/connect, without owner header/bootstrap APIs.

conclusion: Evidence supports actual native Common chain traffic over the owned browser relay route in this configured single-host test. TxQUIC bridge is not an alternative chain downloader in the reviewed paths. Report configuration-based path isolation plus observed browser-mesh peers; do not claim OS-enforced network exclusion or separate physical networks.
namespaceFixtureRecommendation: Not required to establish this change with the stronger exact RTC data proof plus native peer/hash observations. If a future acceptance claim requires proving all other network paths physically impossible, use a separate Common network namespace with no default route and a fixed TLS byte-forwarder to only the configured gateway. Preserve end-to-end TLS hostname verification; bind its other port to the namespace loopback and record netns routes/listeners. This was not executed.
